articles.title: Reducing false alarms in crackmeter-based early warning of small-scale slope deformation via deep learning-driven asynchronous displacement–rainfall data fusion
articles.titleEn: Reducing false alarms in crackmeter-based early warning of small-scale slope deformation via deep learning-driven asynchronous displacement–rainfall data fusion
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Real-time crackmeter-based deformation monitoring systems for small-scale rainfall-affected slopes suffer from high false alarm rates. Across multi-slope monitoring settings, threshold-based alerts are vulnerable to noise, while conventional denoising and prediction-based validation methods remain limited in automated warning discrimination and cross-site generalization. To address this bottleneck, a labeled dataset and a data-driven binary classification framework were developed to distinguish true early warnings from false alarms among threshold-triggered sensor alerts. A multi-source dataset of crack-displacement and rainfall observations was constructed from monitored slopes in Fujian Province, China, with genuine and false alerts labelled based on field investigations and geological expert assessment. A patch-based dual-branch temporally-aware Transformer model was developed to fuse asynchronous multi-rate data, preserve the temporal direction from antecedent rainfall to subsequent displacement, and satisfy stringent real-time decision constraints. By simultaneously capturing long-term rainfall-displacement interactions and high-resolution displacement dynamics, the model outperforms competitive baselines, achieving a precision of 90.32 %, a recall of 89.38 %, and an F 2 -score of 89.54 % in identifying true early warnings. Interpretability analysis reveals that the model's decisions are primarily driven by localized displacement trends and the relationship between rainfall and displacement, aligning with expert judgment. Analyses of misclassified cases informed additional safeguards to further reduce missed warnings. The proposed framework helps reduce false alarms and supports reliable automated slope hazard monitoring. However, the present validation is limited to the Fujian rainfall-triggered monitoring context, and application to other geological or climatic settings requires further external validation and local adaptation.

articles.title: Microclimate, Vegetation, and Soil Response to Micro‐Zonal Solar Photovoltaic Patterning in a Humid Sub‐Tropical Agrivoltaic Grazing System
articles.titleEn: Microclimate, Vegetation, and Soil Response to Micro‐Zonal Solar Photovoltaic Patterning in a Humid Sub‐Tropical Agrivoltaic Grazing System
articles.abstract: Agrivoltaic grazing systems, or the integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) energy generation with livestock grazing, are the most common form of multi‐use solar energy in the United States and much of the world. However, there is a substantial gap in our understanding of the ecological impacts of combining PV and grazing in these novel ecosystems. Addressing this gap, we present data from the first 2 years of a study characterizing the interacting effects of PV infrastructure with land management (sheep grazing and mowing) in the Southeastern US. We observed spatial and temporal solar radiation and precipitation patterning among micro‐zones unique to the humid‐subtropical climate region and found that the PV modules maintained higher soil moisture than in the absence of PV, across all micro‐zones, with more dramatic differences observed during drier periods. Despite the significant patterning of microclimate conditions, we found no significant difference in above‐ground primary productivity across any micro‐zones or between management treatments within the array. Three years after construction, we detected no significant difference in soil carbon stocks across micro‐zones.

articles.title: Manhattan Pluvial Flood Simulations Under Two Extreme Rainfall Scenarios Show Similar Severity Patterns but Contrasting Peak Timing Across Districts
articles.titleEn: Manhattan Pluvial Flood Simulations Under Two Extreme Rainfall Scenarios Show Similar Severity Patterns but Contrasting Peak Timing Across Districts
articles.abstract: Urban pluvial flooding is often summarized by peak depth, peak extent, or cumulative burden, but these metrics do not distinguish when flooding first becomes hazardous from when the hazardous area becomes largest. This study introduces an activation–occupancy framework to quantify these two times and applies it to building‐resolving shallow‐water simulations of Manhattan ( at m resolution) under an Ida‐derived hyetograph and New York City's 1‐hr design storm. Under the Ida‐derived rainfall at the 0.3‐m threshold, district activation peaks occur within a 35‐min span, whereas the times of maximum hazard extent are much more dispersed. Under the shorter design storm, peak timing compresses sharply. Rainfall is spatially uniform in both simulations, so the 35‐min activation spread reflects routing alone and provides a lower bound on the variability of activation timing; spatial rainfall heterogeneity lies outside the modeled scenarios. Across the two modeled rainfall scenarios, severe‐flooding geography remains broadly consistent: the same seven districts exceed the borough reference at 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 m, with the strongest rank preservation for eventual extent and hazardous area–time burden. At 0.5 m, that set contracts to six because Lower East Side/Chinatown falls just below the borough reference in both scenarios. East Harlem remains the principal exception in design‐storm timing at the deeper thresholds. These diagnostics distinguish severity patterns relevant to adaptation from scenario‐specific timing information for warning and response.
articles.abstractEn: Urban pluvial flooding is often summarized by peak depth, peak extent, or cumulative burden, but these metrics do not distinguish when flooding first becomes hazardous from when the hazardous area becomes largest. Under the Ida‐derived rainfall at the 0.3‐m threshold, district activation peaks occur within a 35‐min span, whereas the times of maximum hazard extent are much more dispersed. Under the shorter design storm, peak timing compresses sharply. Rainfall is spatially uniform in both simulations, so the 35‐min activation spread reflects routing alone and provides a lower bound on the variability of activation timing; spatial rainfall heterogeneity lies outside the modeled scenarios. Across the two modeled rainfall scenarios, severe‐flooding geography remains broadly consistent: the same seven districts exceed the borough reference at 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 m, with the strongest rank preservation for eventual extent and hazardous area–time burden. At 0.5 m, that set contracts to six because Lower East Side/Chinatown falls just below the borough reference in both scenarios. East Harlem remains the principal exception in design‐storm timing at the deeper thresholds. These diagnostics distinguish severity patterns relevant to adaptation from scenario‐specific timing information for warning and response.

articles.title: Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
articles.titleEn: Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
articles.abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio‐temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio‐temporal variation. Recent research extends STMs by also estimating density responses to habitat conditions at nearby locations using a “spatially distributed lag” (SDL) that averages habitat conditions in the vicinity of samples. Here, we extend the SDL by incorporating insights from diffusion‐enhanced STMs to simultaneously estimate spatially distributed and time‐lagged responses to nearby and past habitat conditions (a “spatio‐temporal distributed lag” STDL). We then use summer bottom trawl survey data from the eastern Bering Sea (1982–2024) to measure whether spatial and/or temporal lags are parsimonious when predicting population density from temperature anomalies for six ecologically important fishes. Results show that time‐lagged responses are parsimonious, positive, and substantial (correlation of 0.20–0.83 per year) for five species, and that density responses to temperature anomalies also diffuse outward over time for four species at 30–53 km per year. A self‐ and cross‐test simulation experiment shows that model selection can identify the appropriate model and that parameter estimates are approximately unbiased. We therefore conclude that temperature carryover effects arise in marine fishes and implement the method in the R package sdmTMB so that future studies can estimate nonlocal and time‐lagged responses when measuring density responses to habitat.

articles.title: Integrating Information From Hydrologic Models and SWOT Remote Sensing Measurements to Estimate Discharge Across River Networks
articles.titleEn: Integrating Information From Hydrologic Models and SWOT Remote Sensing Measurements to Estimate Discharge Across River Networks
articles.abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite has the potential to improve knowledge of river discharge globally. However, SWOT discharge algorithms are informed by global hydrological model data, and a portion of the model's systematic bias is passed along to the SWOT discharge time series. To address this issue, we present a new algorithm designed to reduce systematic bias in SWOT discharge. The algorithm analytically integrates basin‐scale information by applying mass conservation to time‐averaged SWOT discharge and estimates of regionalized runoff. We test the algorithm on three river basins with drainage areas on the order of 10 5 km 2 . We find that when the time‐averaged SWOT discharge observations are spatially unbiased (i.e., their spatially averaged error is close to zero) the algorithm significantly reduces error in SWOT discharge: the median (interquartile range) absolute value of the normalized error is 15% (10%–19%) for the Willamette River basin, and 12% (7%–48%) for the upper Ohio River basin, significant reduction in SWOT discharge error (median values of 30% and 31%, respectively). However, for the Loire River basin, which has high (∼60%) spatial bias, the algorithm does not reduce error associated with SWOT discharge. These results indicate that understanding and reducing spatial bias at the basin scale is key for reducing time series bias in river discharge. Based on a preliminary assessment of spatial bias globally, we find that SWOT discharge could achieve its target accuracy (30% discharge error, with most of it temporal bias) even in ungaged basins, enabling SWOT discharge to significantly increase accuracies of the global water budget.

articles.title: Coupling MRI and XRCT to Resolve Structure–Transport Evolution During Enzyme‐Induced Calcite Precipitation at the REV Scale
articles.titleEn: Coupling MRI and XRCT to Resolve Structure–Transport Evolution During Enzyme‐Induced Calcite Precipitation at the REV Scale
articles.abstract: The aim of this study is to understand how enzyme‐induced calcite precipitation (EICP) modifies flow and transport in porous media, as this is essential for developing sustainable approaches to soil stabilization, permeability control, and groundwater management. For this, we investigated the coupled evolution of pore structure and hydraulic properties during EICP at the representative elementary volume (REV) scale using a dual non‐invasive imaging approach combining X‐ray computed tomography (XRCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Three replicate sand columns with initial permeabilities between 22 × 10 −12 m 2 and 25 × 10 −12 m 2 were treated with EICP using a constant flow injection and solutions of 0.5 M CaCl 2 , 0.5 M urea, and 5.0 g L −1 jack bean meal. Over six injection cycles (175 pore volumes), permeability decreased by more than three orders of magnitude, while average porosity declined moderately from 0.38 to 0.28. XRCT revealed that precipitation was concentrated near the inlet, where the surface to volume ratio increased from 0.055 to 0.065 μm −1 and tortuosity rose from ∼2.0 to ∼3.5. MRI measurements showed corresponding localized reductions in water content and relaxation times, with T 1 decreasing from ∼1.5 to ∼1.0 s and T 2 from ∼50 to ∼30 ms. The combined imaging results indicate a two‐stage precipitation process with early pore‐throat blockage followed by progressive narrowing of pore bodies. These findings demonstrate that permeability loss is governed not only by porosity reduction but also by precipitation distribution.

articles.title: Storage, Connectivity, and Stream Drying in Headwater Systems: Modeling Across Hydrogeomorphic Features
articles.titleEn: Storage, Connectivity, and Stream Drying in Headwater Systems: Modeling Across Hydrogeomorphic Features
articles.abstract: Headwater streams play a critical role in the physical, chemical, and biological functions of downstream waters. However, predicting their specific impact on a landscape scale remains a grand challenge, prompting the development of the river corridor framework to integrate the study of stream channels and hyporheic zones with that of adjacent hillslopes and riparian zones. To operationalize this framework and better explore hydrologic fluxes, the intermediate hydrogeomorphic feature (HGF) scale was recently defined to discretize the river corridor into quantifiable and repeatable compartments. In this study, we used process‐based modeling within and across HGFs to evaluate hydrologic connectivity, storage, streamflow, and drying. We used the Advanced Terrestrial Simulator to model hydrologic fluxes in an experimental watershed in the Coastal Plain of the southeastern United States, where we delineated incised, intact riparian, and wetland HGFs along three streams. Among HGFs, incised channels gained the most water from the subsurface, wetland HGFs maintained the highest water tables, and intact riparian HGFs frequently went dry. Incised and wetland HGFs generated the majority of discharge throughout the year, but dry season discharge was dominated by streamflow gains in incised HGFs. Together, these results suggest that stream incision increases downstream connectivity and export, whereas wetland HGFs increase watershed capacity for storage. Our findings highlight the role of geomorphic structure in driving spatial patterns of drying, storage, and connectivity. Given the pervasiveness of stream incision across anthropogenically impacted systems, our results provide a basis for identifying locations significant to watershed‐scale hydrologic export or retention.

articles.title: Hysteretic Dynamics of Stream Network Expansion and Contraction Revealed Through High‐Resolution Integrated Hydrological Modeling
articles.titleEn: Hysteretic Dynamics of Stream Network Expansion and Contraction Revealed Through High‐Resolution Integrated Hydrological Modeling
articles.abstract: As landscapes cycle through wetting and drying, stream networks expand and contract, driving material export and biogeochemical transformations with important implications for water quality and ecosystem function. Because it is challenging to measure the extent of the active network, streamflow () is often used as a proxy. However, the relationship remains uncertain, especially for larger catchments where direct observation is labor intensive. Using a process‐based integrated hydrological model capable of resolving inundation patterns at high spatial and temporal resolution, we study the dynamics of network extent for a 75 km 2 watershed and its subcatchments. Without catchment‐specific calibration, simulations using the ATS integrated hydrology model agree well with observed daily stream discharge and observed stream persistency regime (perennial vs. non‐perennial). Simulation results reveal that a unique, synchronous relationship between and exists only for small catchments. Specifically, the synchronous data exhibit substantial scatter due to hysteresis, which increases with increasing catchment size. However, a robust relationship free of hysteresis emerges when asynchronous event‐scale peaks of and are considered instead. The event‐scale asynchronous relationship is well approximated as power‐law over the range of peak simulated and remains consistent across nested catchments of varying size, independent of antecedent wetness, season, and storm details. In baseflow conditions, the scaling is also well approximated with a power law but with a larger exponent, suggesting different runoff generation mechanisms. These results offer a more robust framework for understanding stream expansion and contraction in larger, more complex basins.

articles.title: Shallow Cumulus Cloud Statistics in Real‐Case Large‐Eddy Simulations and Their Dependence on Soil Moisture
articles.titleEn: Shallow Cumulus Cloud Statistics in Real‐Case Large‐Eddy Simulations and Their Dependence on Soil Moisture
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: The ability of weather and climate models to reproduce the statistical properties of shallow cumulus clouds (SCCs) is critical for representing boundary‐layer transport, cloud cover, and cloud‐radiative effects. This study investigates statistical properties of SCC ensembles using the Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic model in large‐eddy simulation mode for three cases during the Field Experiment on Submesoscale Spatio‐Temporal Variability in Lindenberg campaign. Feature‐based tracking is applied to identify cloud objects and track their evolution. Each cloud is classified as active or passive according to its in‐cloud buoyancy excess. The cloud‐base mass flux distribution of each class is robustly captured by a Weibull distribution. Active clouds exhibit shape parameters , consistent with convective memory related to their life‐cycle, while passive clouds approach , indicating stochastic, short‐lived nature. The bulk cloud‐base mass flux , representing the convective transport of the SCC population, scales linearly with surface heat input per unit cloud moist‐static‐energy excess, weighted by thermodynamic efficiency of the surface‐driven moist heat cycle. This scaling emerges primarily across the soil‐moisture perturbations and holds from moderately moisture‐limited to energy‐limited regimes, but linearity breaks down under very dry conditions, where a suppressed evaporative fraction and the resulting sub‐cloud moisture deficit prevent further increases in . Soil moisture strongly controls cloud number, updraft strength, cloud size, and the mass‐flux distribution, whereas responds to both soil‐moisture perturbations and day‐to‐day large‐scale conditions, highlighting land‐atmosphere coupling as a key regulator of shallow convective variability over land.

articles.title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
articles.titleEn: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
articles.abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.

articles.title: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
articles.titleEn: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
articles.abstract: Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. To this end, we conduct 100,000-year-long simulations for different CO 2 conditions using the community Earth system model coupled to the bihemispheric Penn State University ice sheet–ice shelf model. Whereas global warming exceeding 2 °C above pre-industrial conditions and related subsurface ocean warming lead to the millennial-scale disintegration of the West Antarctic ice sheet, the East Antarctic ice sheet shows a much greater resilience, even at 10 °C or more of warming. The simulations reveal that a moister and cloudier atmosphere over Antarctica, with southward-shifted westerlies, increases snow accumulation and reduces shortwave radiation. For Greenland, a 6 °C threshold above pre-industrial levels is identified. Capturing the balance of ocean- and atmosphere-driven ablation and accumulation processes in coupled climate–ice-sheet models will improve projections of long-term sea-level rise.

articles.title: How Water Resource Tax Reform Shapes Corporate Green Investment: Evidence From Financing Capacity and Investment Willingness
articles.titleEn: How Water Resource Tax Reform Shapes Corporate Green Investment: Evidence From Financing Capacity and Investment Willingness
articles.abstract: Water scarcity poses an increasingly severe challenge to sustainable economic development, yet empirical evidence remains limited on how environmental taxation affects corporate green investment (GI) decisions and the micro‐level mechanisms through which these effects operate. Using Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2010 to 2024, this study exploits the 2017 expansion of China's water resource tax reform, a single policy shock varying across regions and industries, and applies a triple‐difference strategy to identify the causal effect of the policy on corporate GI. The results show that water resource tax reform significantly increases corporate GI, and this conclusion remains robust across robustness tests. Mechanism analysis reveals two complementary transmission channels. Extended analysis further shows that the GI induced by the reform simultaneously increases total factor productivity and reduces water pollution equivalents, supporting the win‐win logic of the Porter hypothesis. These findings provide empirical evidence for improving the design of green fiscal and tax policies.

articles.title: Design and trial implementation of a continental-scale, kilometre-resolution hourly precipitation analysis for Australia using satellite, radar and gauges
articles.titleEn: Design and trial implementation of a continental-scale, kilometre-resolution hourly precipitation analysis for Australia using satellite, radar and gauges
articles.abstract: High-resolution precipitation information is essential for hydrometeorological applications such as extreme weather monitoring, flood forecasting, and disaster risk management. Despite substantial advances in satellite, radar, and gauge observations, producing kilometre-resolution sub-daily precipitation analyses over continental domains remains challenging due to heterogeneous data availability, scale mismatches, and computational constraints. This study presents the design and trial implementation of BRAIN (blended rainfall), a continental-scale, kilometre-resolution hourly precipitation analysis for Australia. In this initial implementation, BRAIN integrates three key data sources from the Australian Bureau of Meteorology: geostationary satellite rainfall estimates (2 km, 10 min) from Himawari, radar rainfall estimates (1 km, 5 min) from the national radar network, and rainfall observations from sub-daily rain gauges. The trialled system incorporates quality control, spatiotemporal aggregation, bias correction, and a simplified statistical interpolation configuration designed to balance analysis performance and computational scalability at the continental scale. Source contributions are weighted according to their spatial and temporal error characteristics, allowing each data type to influence the analysis where it is most informative. The initial implementation produces hourly rainfall fields at 2 km resolution across the Australian continent. Evaluation over the 2022–2023 trial period indicates that the blended analysis improves overall upon satellite-only, radar-only, and satellite–gauge products. Comparisons with gauge-based interpolation and the current daily operational product further illustrate the spatial characteristics of the blended analysis, including finer-scale rainfall structures and intensity variations that are not represented by these products. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed design for continental-scale, high-resolution multi-source precipitation analysis in the Australian context, with potential applications to long-term historical reconstruction and near-real-time rainfall analysis. The flexible and scalable system design also allows future upgrades, including finer spatial and temporal resolutions and the incorporation of additional data sources. Beyond Australia, this study provides a practical reference for developing large-scale multi-source precipitation analyses at kilometre and hourly resolutions.

articles.title: Deploying machine learning components coupled to Earth System Models with OASIS3-MCT (v6) and Eophis (v1.1)
articles.titleEn: Deploying machine learning components coupled to Earth System Models with OASIS3-MCT (v6) and Eophis (v1.1)
articles.abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) components into Earth System Models (ESMs) holds significant potential for improving climate simulations, but it is often constrained by challenges related to interoperability, reproducibility, and computational efficiency. This paper presents a novel coupler-based approach that combines the OASIS3-MCT coupling library with Eophis, a high-performance Python library, to seamlessly deploy ML components in ESMs. By leveraging OASIS3-MCT’s robust communication infrastructure, Eophis abstracts the technical complexities of coupling, enabling users to integrate Python-based ML models or analytical parameterizations into geophysical simulations. Eophis provides a modular interface for defining data exchanges, synchronizing time steps, and supporting parallel communications, including advanced features such as halo construction for Convolutional Neural Networks and hybrid CPU/GPU execution. We evaluate this framework by coupling the NEMO4 ocean model with both ML-based and analytical parameterizations, demonstrating scalability, asynchronous execution, and flexible resource allocation. Benchmarking results show that this approach allows for deploying Python scripts in NEMO without affecting time-to-solution, provided extra computing resources are adequately allocated. The combination of OASIS3-MCT and Eophis offers a user-friendly solution for hybrid modelling, which facilitates the integration of ML components into ESM workflows. By lowering the barrier to hybrid modeling, this work facilitates the integration of ML components into ESM workflows. The combination of OASIS3-MCT and Eophis offers a practical solution for bridging the gap between ML and climate modeling, supporting innovation in Earth system science while maintaining reproducibility and ease of use.

articles.title: Towards high-fidelity simulations of coastal submesoscale baroclinic instabilities with MPAS-O (vE3SM3.0.0) – Part 1: Idealized experiments
articles.titleEn: Towards high-fidelity simulations of coastal submesoscale baroclinic instabilities with MPAS-O (vE3SM3.0.0) – Part 1: Idealized experiments
articles.abstract: Rapid advances in computational power over the past decade have enabled global, kilometer-scale simulations that realistically represent open-ocean submesoscale dynamics. However, the ability of global ocean models to represent coastal submesoscale dynamics – where flows are more heterogeneous and strongly shaped by coastlines, bathymetry, and buoyancy inputs – remains largely unexplored. This study is the first of two companion papers comparing coastal submesoscale processes representation in two models with very different numerical approaches: MPAS-O, an unstructured grid global ocean model, and ROMS, a structured grid regional model. This study is the first idealized evaluation of MPAS-O’s representation of coastal submesoscale dynamics using observed conditions in the Mississippi-Atchafalaya (M-A) River plume as a template for initial conditions, with the previously validated ROMS model serving as a benchmark. An important motivation for this study is to examine the suitability of models designed for global ocean simulations in reproducing energetic coastal flows. We compare statistical metrics based on flow invariants – total strain, relative vorticity, and divergence – as well as velocity gradients in frontal coordinates, across horizontal resolutions ranging from 10 km to 100 m within an idealized model domain. We find that the representation of submesoscale baroclinic instabilities is highly similar across all resolutions such that the impact of model choice is smaller than the choice of spatial grid resolution. We also compare numerical and physical mixing between models using online diagnostics based on discrete variance decay. We find that ROMS generally has more numerical mixing and less physical mixing than MPAS-O across all resolutions. Trends in numerical mixing likely arise from MPAS-O's flux-corrected transport tracer advection scheme, which exhibits a stronger variance-producing response relative to the MPDATA scheme used in the ROMS simulations. Trends in physical mixing likely arise from differences in each model’s configuration of the vertical mixing scheme (the K-Profile Parameterization). A companion paper extends this idealized model-model comparison to realistic simulations of the M-A River plume.

articles.title: Nitrous oxide dynamics across nitrogen and pH gradients in headwater streams
articles.titleEn: Nitrous oxide dynamics across nitrogen and pH gradients in headwater streams
articles.abstract: Headwater streams in agricultural landscapes can contribute substantially to nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions, yet the environmental controls on stream N 2 O dynamics remain poorly resolved, particularly in systems with low pH. We investigated 72 Danish headwater streams spanning broad gradients in pH (5.0–8.8), land use, and soil type to identify the main drivers of N 2 O variability. Nitrate (NO3-) was the strongest predictor of N 2 O saturation, and its positive association with N 2 O intensified under acidic conditions according to linear mixed models. In the same model, ammonium, dissolved organic carbon, and stream depth also showed significant but weaker positive relationships with N 2 O. Spatial differences among streams explained considerably more variation than seasonal or regional patterns, underscoring the dominance of local factors. Streams with pH 6 consistently exhibited higher N 2 O saturation, and generalized additive modelling indicated a marked decline in N 2 O levels beginning near pH 6. Despite generally high N 2 O saturation, approximately 9 % of observations displayed undersaturation, which occurred mainly in streams with low NO3- concentrations and across all seasons. Our results indicate that acidic, weakly buffered catchments may enhance in-stream N 2 O accumulation even at moderate nitrogen levels. These findings highlight the need to consider pH-related controls when assessing N 2 O dynamics in freshwater networks and when designing mitigation strategies for agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: The open uncertainty window in ocean biogeochemical responses to fossil carbon emissions
articles.titleEn: The open uncertainty window in ocean biogeochemical responses to fossil carbon emissions
articles.abstract: Automated parameter optimisation can effectively reduce model-data mismatch and provide information about ocean biogeochemistry parameter sensitivities, but to what extent it reduces uncertainty in responses to climate change is not well understood. To explore the robustness of simulated ocean biogeochemical responses to a “business-as-usual” RCP 8.5-equivalent fossil CO 2 emission scenario until year 2300, six biogeochemical parameters are optimised against contemporary oxygen, phosphate, and nitrate fields in three different physical configurations of the UVic ESCM. The phytoplankton maximum growth rate parameter value and the nitrogen-to-oxygen molar ratio of organic matter remineralisation were found to be robust across the calibration ensemble, with the former varying less than 1.6 % across the calibrated ensemble and the latter varying less than 4 %. While each calibrated model performs nearly equivalently in terms of optimal total misfit (a result of the model calibration objective), significant differences in biogeochemical fluxes and rates (e.g., global net primary and particulate organic carbon; POC) remain. Application of CO 2 emissions to the calibrated models to the year 2300 produces model responses that start diverging in global average trends in the early 2000s. Models with more sluggish pre-industrial circulations respond less to climate warming in terms of physical changes, but more in their primary production (as these models have been tuned to have weaker limitation on production). Models that have larger changes in circulation metrics due to anthropogenic CO 2 emissions, in particular the Southern Ocean overturning, demonstrate larger changes in shallow (130 m) and deep (2 km) POC fluxes (due to stronger parametric control on particle flux). Suboxic volume trends are smaller in models with larger changes to the physical circulation metrics owing to compensation between model tuning favouring strong biological oxygen consumption in their vigorous pre-industrial state and these models' having a greater physical sensitivity to warming. By the year 2300, the resulting model responses vary by a factor 2.8 in net primary production, 5 in shallow POC fluxes, 1.7 in deep POC fluxes, 1.5 in nitrogen fixation and 1.2 in suboxic volume, but the model spread in absolute values relative to the pre-industrial remains largely unchanged, demonstrating the utility of constraining the pre-industrial ocean state in diverse model ensembles for robust projections of ocean change. However, an uncertainty window remains open in ocean biogeochemical responses to CO 2 emissions, despite systematic tuning.

articles.title: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
articles.titleEn: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Flood frequency analysis (FFA) is essential for flood risk management and infrastructure design, yet estimates of flood quantiles remain strongly influenced by the length and representativeness of available streamflow record. We introduce UQ-flood, a process-based flood-frequency framework that integrates a stochastic weather generator, a process-based hydrologic model, and a residual error model developed at the annual-maximum scale. The framework explicitly addresses the presence of errors in simulated annual flood peaks generated by models calibrated to continuous streamflow data. We apply UQ-flood to three Canadian watersheds with contrasting hydroclimatic conditions using 30 years of meteorological and streamflow observations. Long-record empirical annual-maximum estimates provide the primary benchmark, while Bayesian Generalized Extreme Value estimates based on short and long records provide secondary statistical benchmarks for the central flood-quantile estimates. Across the three watersheds, the central UQ-flood estimates remained within the confidence intervals for the long-record discharge quantiles, although their relative proximity to the empirical estimates varied by watershed and return period. Process-based simulations without residual-error correction systematically underestimated flood magnitudes, whereas applying the residual error model shifted the estimated flood-frequency curves toward the long-record observational benchmarks. The framework also propagates residual predictive variability directly at the annual-maximum scale. These results demonstrate that annual-maximum residual error modelling can correct for systematic discrepancies in process-based flood estimates and support central flood-quantile estimation even at sites with short data records.

articles.title: The 2025 Mediterranean marine heatwaves through sea surface temperature analogues
articles.titleEn: The 2025 Mediterranean marine heatwaves through sea surface temperature analogues
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: The Mediterranean Sea experienced an exceptional marine heatwave throughout June–July 2025. Here we analyse this event using an analogue framework that differs from the common atmospheric circulation-based analogue attribution approach. Instead of identifying atmospheric circulation analogues first, we search directly for historical analogues of the observed sea surface temperature (SST) anomaly pattern of the 20 to 30 June 2025 build-up and peak phase, and then compare the associated atmospheric and air-sea surface conditions in a past (1950 to 1986) and a present (1987 to 2024) period, using ERA5 daily fields over the Mediterranean between June and September. Our results suggest that the present period exhibits higher SST anomalies than the past one, with the strongest positive differences over the western Mediterranean and the Adriatic Sea. Warmer 2 m air temperatures over surrounding land areas and higher net shortwave radiation over large parts of the basin are also observed, while sea level pressure, wind speed, latent heat flux, sensible heat flux, and longwave radiation display smaller and more spatially heterogeneous changes. Thus, the 2025 event occurred in a warmer thermodynamic background than analogous SST patterns in earlier decades. Since the analogue framework cannot fully separate externally forced trends from internal variability and it does not explicitly resolve ocean dynamical processes, these results do not constitute a complete formal attribution on their own. Nevertheless, the analogue analysis supports the interpretation that long term warming contributed substantially to the intensity of the 2025 Mediterranean marine heatwave and shows how SST analogue comparisons can complement existing attribution approaches for marine extremes.

articles.title: Multi-data source based quantifying urban flood severity in major Chinese cities (2000–2024) using a hybrid machine-learning weighting framework
articles.titleEn: Multi-data source based quantifying urban flood severity in major Chinese cities (2000–2024) using a hybrid machine-learning weighting framework
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Urban flooding poses a critical challenge to sustainable urban development, yet long-term comparative assessments remain limited by fragmented and heterogeneous disaster records. To address this gap, this study integrates multi-source flood-event data from 20 major Chinese cities during 2000–2024 and develops an impact-based framework for assessing urban flood severity. Official statistics, news reports, and social media records are combined to construct an event-level flood database, which supports the development of a Flood Severity Index (FSI). A hybrid weighting framework that combines conventional weighting schemes with machine-learning-assisted indicator attribution is developed to improve the robustness and interpretability of severity assessment. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity: southern cities exhibit higher average severity levels and more frequent high-severity events, whereas northern cities generally show lower baseline severity but remain vulnerable to episodic extreme flood impacts. Temporal analysis indicates substantial interannual variability rather than a consistent long-term increasing or decreasing trend. These findings highlight the need for region-specific flood management strategies, including reducing persistent high-severity impacts in southern cities and improving preparedness for abrupt extreme events in northern cities. This study demonstrates the value of integrating fragmented historical records into a comparable framework for urban flood severity assessment.

articles.title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
articles.titleEn: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
articles.abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. articles.title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
articles.titleEn: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
articles.abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth’s history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO 2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth’s habitability.

articles.title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
articles.titleEn: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
articles.abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

articles.title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
articles.titleEn: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
articles.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

articles.title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
articles.titleEn: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
articles.abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in Escherichia coli combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph Bacillus methanolicus partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

articles.title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
articles.titleEn: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
articles.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

articles.title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
articles.titleEn: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
articles.abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

articles.title: Monsoon zonal seesaw: Development of the South Asian monsoon aridified North Africa in the Cenozoic
articles.titleEn: Monsoon zonal seesaw: Development of the South Asian monsoon aridified North Africa in the Cenozoic
articles.abstract: North Africa experienced a pronounced transition from humid to arid conditions during the early Cenozoic. Meanwhile, the South Asian monsoon underwent substantial intensification, largely driven by the uplift of the Himalayan-Tibetan Plateau. Here, we demonstrate that the two events, which greatly shaped the paleoenvironment and modern regional climate, are not independent responses to paleogeography changes; rather, the former is primarily driven by the latter through the monsoon-desert mechanism, in which South Asian monsoon diabatic heating produces large-scale subsidence and aridity over North Africa. Using multiple ensembles of paleoclimate simulations and a model for the atmospheric response to imposed diabatic heating, we show that the intensification and poleward shift of Asian monsoon rainfall each make comparable contributions to the aridification of North Africa. Our findings identify a persistent dynamical pathway linking the South Asian and North African monsoons and suggest that it played a major role in early Cenozoic North African aridification, while its climatic expression at other times depended on the relative strengths of competing forcings.

articles.title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
articles.titleEn: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
articles.abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.

articles.title: SLAMS‐2.0: A Stochastic, Lagrangian Particle‐Resolving Modeling Framework for Investigating the Biological Carbon Pump
articles.titleEn: SLAMS‐2.0: A Stochastic, Lagrangian Particle‐Resolving Modeling Framework for Investigating the Biological Carbon Pump
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Sinking biogenic particles drive the ocean biological carbon pump (BCP), yet the processes governing their formation, transformation, and fate remain poorly constrained and are difficult to represent with existing modeling frameworks. Traditional approaches either resolve particle populations as bulk distributions or simulate individual particles at high computational cost, limiting their ability to capture both particle‐scale processes and emergent particulate fluxes. Here we present SLAMS‐2.0, a stochastic, particle‐resolving Lagrangian framework that bridges particle‐based and population‐based approaches by explicitly simulating individual, heterogeneous particles and their probabilistic interactions while efficiently capturing the evolving particle population across the full size spectrum through a “superparticle” formulation. The model combines this approach with observation‐informed BCP process representations, allowing particle composition, microstructure, and interactions to emerge dynamically from first‐principles fractal scaling and stochastic encounter dynamics. SLAMS‐2.0 is evaluated at six open‐ocean time‐series sites spanning contrasting biogeographical regimes against a wide range of observations, including particulate organic carbon (POC) and biogenic mineral fluxes, particle abundances, and size distributions. We show that carbon packaging, porosity, mineral ballast, and aggregation efficiency—rather than particle size or sinking velocity alone—govern POC flux transfer to depth, with large, porous, ballast‐rich aggregates driving deep‐ocean POC flux. SLAMS‐2.0 provides a framework for investigating how particle physicochemical attributes and interactions shape emergent carbon fluxes, with applications to both observational process studies and the development of improved biogeochemical model representations.

articles.title: More Frequent, Faster, and Seasonally Reorganized Drought‐to‐Pluvial Transitions in U.S. Cities
articles.titleEn: More Frequent, Faster, and Seasonally Reorganized Drought‐to‐Pluvial Transitions in U.S. Cities
articles.abstract: Hydroclimatic variability is projected to intensify under continued warming, yet the evolving likelihood, rapidness, and seasonal timing of drought‐to‐pluvial transitions remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a probabilistic framework that integrates a severity‐resolved Markov formulation to estimate conditional drought‐to‐pluvial transition probabilities, Event Coincidence Analysis to quantify Relief Time (TR; the interval between drought amelioration and subsequent pluvial onset), and circular statistics to characterize the seasonal timing of post‐drought pluvial occurrence. We apply this framework to the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index derived from a 20‐member ensemble of downscaled climate‐model projections for 27 U.S. cities representing all nine National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Climate Regions. Results reveal a systematic reorganization of drought‐to‐pluvial dynamics under future warming. For severe drought thresholds, drought‐to‐pluvial transitions increase by approximately 132%–154%, while severe drought states increase by 128%–203% relative to historical conditions. Across most cities, Relief Time shortens by 0.1–0.3 months, indicating increasingly abrupt transitions from drought to wet conditions. Seasonal timing also reorganizes, with the first post‐drought pluvial event shifting by approximately 1–3 months in many regions. Joint changes in transition probability and TR reveal distinct regional acceleration regimes characterized by increasing transition frequency, increasing abruptness, or both. The findings indicate that future drought recovery may increasingly occur through faster, more frequent, and seasonally altered transitions to wet conditions. The proposed framework provides transferable metrics for diagnosing drought‐to‐pluvial behavior and offers actionable insights for flood‐risk assessment, water‐resource management, and climate adaptation under a warming climate.

articles.title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
articles.titleEn: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
articles.abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

articles.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
articles.titleEn: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
articles.abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

articles.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
articles.titleEn: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
articles.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

articles.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
articles.titleEn: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
articles.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

articles.title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
articles.titleEn: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
articles.abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

articles.title: When AI takes away the thrill of discovery
articles.titleEn: When AI takes away the thrill of discovery
articles.abstract: “Pure math is being devastated or revolutionized, depending on your point of view.” So said Cornell professor Steven Strogatz after the artificial intelligence (AI) company OpenAI announced in early September a potential solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems that represent the highest goals for mathematical proofs. OpenAI’s solution involved unleashing an army of AI agents at a cost of millions of dollars in computing power, and it also certainly drew on decades of human effort in mathematics before it. Then a few weeks later, OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts describing progress on 372 mathematical problem families, and Google DeepMind published (in Science ) solutions from their own AI math system. These events are potentially exciting for those who long to know the answers to these problems as soon as possible, but they have also sent the world of mathematics reeling, and pose an even bigger question for all fields: Can the satisfaction of understanding ever replace the thrill of discovery?

articles.title: Economic Principles and Optimal Rules for Flood Detention Basin Operation
articles.titleEn: Economic Principles and Optimal Rules for Flood Detention Basin Operation
articles.abstract: Flood detention basins (FDBs) are critical infrastructure for mitigating downstream flood risk through temporary floodwater storage and are widely implemented globally. However, with ongoing economic development within FDBs, balancing the safety of downstream flood protected areas with the internal economic losses of FDBs is a significant challenge, requiring a fundamental theory and quantitative rules for optimizing the flood diversion operations. This study develops a theoretical optimization model for FDB operation. We analytically derive economic principles for the optimal allocation of flood discharge between the FDB and the downstream protected area for various inflow cases with corresponding optimal rules proposed. A key control indicator is derived, named the Risk‐Adjusted Safety Threshold for the downstream protected area, which governs the activation and magnitude of flood diversion. We verify that the proposed optimal rules can reduce the total economic losses in a real FDB case in China. Additionally, the effects of key parameters, including physical constraints, hydrologic forecast uncertainty and economic losses, on optimal operation effectiveness are explored. The proposed economic principles and optimal rules for FDB operation can also offer valuable insights for flood risk management across various areas.

articles.title: Enhancing Groundwater Contaminant Transport Forecasts Through Synergy of Machine Learning and Physics‐Based Models
articles.titleEn: Enhancing Groundwater Contaminant Transport Forecasts Through Synergy of Machine Learning and Physics‐Based Models
articles.abstract: Groundwater is vital for water supply, irrigation, and environmental sustainability, yet contamination remains a global challenge. Remediation of contaminated aquifers is hindered by difficulties in tracking contaminant spread and identifying pollutant sources. Although advances in aquifer characterization have improved groundwater modeling, limitations persist in capturing spatial heterogeneity and accurately predicting contaminant transport. This work presents a hybrid modeling framework integrating a physics‐based travel‐time model with a multi‐output feed‐forward Deep Neural Network (DNN) to parametrize local BreakThrough Curves (BTCs) at sampling and compliance locations. Focusing on local concentration breakthrough curves rather than hydraulic head or distributed aquifer properties, the method better captures the effects of spatial variations in hydraulic conductivity on the dynamics of the contaminant plume. Model performance was evaluated at different levels of information, and extended to ungauged locations to assess generalization capability. The DNN accurately infers spatially variable transport parameters, with Wasserstein distances consistently lower than those of the moments‐based benchmark when concentration data are sufficient. Performance degrades gradually with reduced data, yet our hybrid approach is less impacted by partial sampling of the BTCs than the traditional moments‐based methods. DNN‐inferred parameters performed better than ensemble‐mean BTC predictions, demonstrating the added value of site‐specific inference in capturing local concentration dynamics that ensemble statistics fail to reproduce. This robustness is attributed to the physical constraints embedded in the transport model and to the cross‐regime learning capability of the DNN, establishing the proposed framework as a practical tool for subsurface characterization under typical field monitoring conditions.

articles.title: High-resolution mapping of pluvial flooding in ungauged agricultural catchments
articles.titleEn: High-resolution mapping of pluvial flooding in ungauged agricultural catchments
articles.abstract: Accurate pluvial flood mapping in ungauged agricultural catchments is often constrained by a lack of calibration data. This study evaluates a parsimonious, high-resolution (1 m) distributed framework assessing peak discharge along concentrated flow paths, validated against 39 events recorded at two nested outlets (84 and 111 ha) of a single experimental catchment. The framework decouples the rainfall-runoff process to systematically compare adjusted Soil Conservation Service Curve Number (SCS-CN) formulations against two spatially explicit routing algorithms (SCS velocity method vs. Simulator for Water Resources in Rural Basins, SWRRB). Within this specific local context, findings demonstrate that the Jain initial abstraction method significantly reduces volumetric bias, with the distributed approach statistically outperforming lumped modelling. However, performance remains strictly regime-dependent, driven by rainfall intensity rather than total depth. This exposes the structural limits of static Curve Number (CN) parameterizations in capturing rapid Hortonian dynamics, causing the model to dampen minor events while amplifying high-intensity storms. Regarding hydraulic transfer, both routing strategies yield statistically equivalent performance (median Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) values of 0.35 vs. 0.34). Crucially, while the routing phase acts as a mechanical propagator of volumetric uncertainty, it effectively synchronizes the overall runoff window. Applied to 25- and 100-year design storms, this framework illustrates hydrodynamic attenuation and kinematic synchronization at confluences. While primarily validated on a single well-monitored catchment, these findings illustrate the approach's potential to pinpoint hydraulic hotspots, with initial benchmarks indicating promising scalability to larger agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: Enhancing hydrological representation of the Brahmaputra basin through terrestrial water storage and surface soil moisture Data Assimilation
articles.titleEn: Enhancing hydrological representation of the Brahmaputra basin through terrestrial water storage and surface soil moisture Data Assimilation
articles.abstract: Understanding the dynamics of terrestrial water storage (TWS), and its components such as surface soil moisture (SSM) and groundwater, is important for the Brahmaputra River basin, where water resources are expected to experience increasing demand and are highly vulnerable to extreme hydrological events and climate change. However, water storage dynamics are complex and difficult to capture by state-of-the-art large-scale hydrological models. In this study, we implement a multi-variate daily TWS and daily SSM sequential Data Assimilation (DA) to integrate the satellite observations in the World Wide Water Resources Assessment model (W3RA) with the aim of improving model-derived water storage dynamics. In our methodology, we propose a model space covariance localization approach that is compared with three other approaches used in the previous literature. The results show that this new approach is the only one to effectively reduce cross-variable influences along the vertical water storage profile, which have been reported as one of the main challenges of multi-variate land DA. A validation of the multi-variate DA estimates (for the period 2004–2015) indicates that more realistic decadal trend and inter-annual variability are introduced into the TWS and groundwater estimates, increasing the correlation coefficients with the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index and observed groundwater levels by +0.24 to +0.54 correlation points. With respect to SSM, DA induces a general phase shift, especially around mountain areas. Improved land water storage estimates reveal a land water decline of 70.9 GT per decade for the period 2004–2015 in the Brahmaputra River basin, which constitutes approximately half of the TWS decline in that period, with the other half caused by glacier retreat (67.5 GT per decade).

articles.title: EnsAI: an emulator for atmospheric ammonia ensembles
articles.titleEn: EnsAI: an emulator for atmospheric ammonia ensembles
articles.abstract: Ensemble-based methods for data assimilation and emissions inversions are a popular way to encode flow-dependency within the model error covariance. While most ensemble methods do not require the use of an adjoint model, the need to repeatedly run a geophysical model to generate the ensemble can be a significant computational burden. In this paper, we introduce EnsAI , a new AI-based ensemble generation system for surface ammonia concentrations. When trained on an ensemble for ammonia generated by the GEM-MACH air quality model, it was shown that the ensembles produced by EnsAI can accurately reproduce the meteorology-dependent features of the original ensemble, while generating the ensemble 3300 times faster than the original GEM-MACH ensemble. While EnsAI requires an upfront cost for generating the ensemble used for training, as well as the training itself, the long term computational savings can greatly exceed these initial computational costs. When used in an emissions inversion system, EnsAI produced similar inversion results to those in which the original GEM-MACH ensemble was used while using significantly less computational resources.

articles.title: Using a two-stage Rosenbrock solver to increase computational efficiency in the DOE's Exascale Earth System Model version 1 (E3SMv1)
articles.titleEn: Using a two-stage Rosenbrock solver to increase computational efficiency in the DOE's Exascale Earth System Model version 1 (E3SMv1)
articles.abstract: The integration of stiff atmospheric chemical systems is a major computational cost in Earth System Models and poses challenges for numerical stability as chemical complexity and temporal resolution increase. In this study, we implement a semi-implicit two-stage Rosenbrock method (ROS2) in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 1 (E3SMv1) and evaluate it as an alternative chemistry time-integration scheme. ROS2 is tested with two interactive chemical mechanisms of substantially different size: chemUCI (60 prognostic species) and trop_strat_mozart_mam4 (155 prognostic species). Numerical experiments include short simulations to quantify computational cost, a box-model timestep-refinement analysis, and one-year integrations to examine numerical stability and solution sensitivity. At the same 180 s chemistry timestep, ROS2 requires approximately 33 % less chemistry integration time than the original iterative implicit solver on the tested Cori/KNL CPU platform. The magnitude of this speedup is configuration dependent. Global-mean surface-ozone differences among the tested configurations are small (≤ 1.03 ppb), and the one-year integrations show no evidence of numerical instability. Spatial and diurnal differences in ozone, NO, NO 2 , and OH are species- and mechanism-dependent, indicating sensitivity to both timestep and solver formulation rather than a common systematic bias. These results support ROS2 as a lower-cost alternative to the current implicit integrator when E3SM chemistry is operated at short timesteps; additional timestep-refinement tests and benchmarking on contemporary CPU/GPU systems are needed to quantify coupled-model convergence and performance portability.
